summary: Christmas hero episode on John Brown, the Calvinist abolitionist who sheltered escaped slaves, killed pro-slavery settlers in Bleeding Kansas and was hanged in 1859 after his raid on the Harpers Ferry armory.

evidence.note: Brown's birth in Torrington, Connecticut in 1800 opens the biography
multi-minute segment on Nat Turner's 1831 revolt and the reprisals that followed
family's strict Calvinism and Brown's Sabbath rules discussed at length
Bleeding Kansas framed as a civil war over slavery; Brown leads a guerrilla militia
Pottawatomie Creek killings of five pro-slavery men in 1856, debated as terrorism
Chatham, Canada constitutional convention of 1858; freed slaves later ferried to Canada
Brown hanged in December 1859 after the failed Harpers Ferry raid

notes: Hero episode; Sophie Lichterman is the in-studio guest for the whole episode, so listed per earlier records. Child abuse here is Brown's harsh whipping of his own children (a few minutes). Harpers Ferry raid gets only a short segment, so it is a keyword, not a subject. Brief modern legacy (Van Spronsen) is a coda, not reaches_present.
